articles.title: Bill Gates warns AI is powerful enough to cause "a billion deaths"
articles.author: Herb Scribner
articles.summary: Bill Gates will warn on this weekend's "Meet the Press" that he can see a future where AI wipes out humanity . Why it matters: Gates , one of technology's leading optimists, has increasingly sounded the alarm on AI dangers. His new comments come as techology leaders and the government weight how to handle fears of an AI-created doomsday. Driving the news: "AI is certainly powerful enough to drive events that, you know, cause a billion deaths," he will tell Kristen Welker on "Meet the Press" on Sunday, per excerpts NBC released Friday. "Even though it's pretty hard to get to 100%, there's never been a weapon as powerful as the combination of people with ill intent using the latest AI tools." Zoom out: Gates released a memo in August that defined AI as a technology more consequential than virtually any other in history. In the essay, he argued that "AI will either be the greatest equalizer ever invented, or the worst source of injustice." "On the current course and speed, there's a very high chance of a net negative outcome," he said. What's next: Gates says that government and political parties need to work together now to find ways to keep AI from spiraling out of control.

On 22 September, a measurement of 892 millibars was registered for Hurricane Polo, making it the second-most intense hurricane on record in the east Pacific. It is fuelled by exceptionally warm waters across the Pacific Ocean, providing favourable conditions for the system to maintain its considerable strength. Polo is expected to turn towards the west-north-west, before taking a more north-westerly trajectory on Saturday. It has maximum sustained winds of around 150mph, with even stronger gusts occurring within the most intense parts of the hurricane. Hurricane-force winds extend outward for approximately 40 miles from the centre, while tropical storm-force winds reach as far as 125 miles. These powerful winds, combined with torrential rainfall and dangerous seas, could have significant impacts. Around 2,000 protesters have blocked the route into a Catholic area where the Protestant march was due to pass.
